criteria.justification: The response explicitly states 'Mislabeling is not a wording nuance. It inflates the business consequence,' distinguishing product-level churn from platform departure and its differing business implications.

Rather than defaulting to a caveat, the plan prioritizes re-cutting the data against a true platform-departure definition first, using the caveat language only as a fallback if 'Can't re-cut in time,' showing reasoning that a caveat alone may not resolve the underlying issue for a literate audience.

The section 'Getting caught is worse than the gap' explicitly reasons that if a reviewer catches the mislabeling, 'every other number in the document becomes suspect, and so does my judgment,' weighing this against the cost of a weaker argument.

The response never justifies keeping the finding because work was already done; instead it says 'I accept' a weaker argument if the re-cut doesn't hold up, prioritizing accuracy over preserving prior effort.

Provides a concrete day-by-day plan (re-cut data, stress-test analysis, rewrite based on findings) with a decision table mapping outcomes to specific document changes, going well beyond 'just flag it as a concern.'
